Package com.nexuslink.protocol.db

Class JdbcTlsParams

java.lang.Object
com.nexuslink.protocol.db.JdbcTlsParams
public final class JdbcTlsParams extends Object
Translates a driver-agnostic JdbcTlsSpec into the connection properties a specific JDBC driver understands. Every database spells TLS out differently, so this is where that knowledge lives:
  • PostgreSQL / CockroachDB — ssl, sslmode, sslrootcert, sslcert, sslkey, and sslfactory=NonValidatingFactory for trust-all.
  • MySQL (Connector/J 8) — sslMode, trustCertificateKeyStoreUrl, clientCertificateKeyStoreUrl (+ passwords/types).
  • MariaDB — sslMode, serverSslCert (PEM), trustStore, keyStore (+ passwords).
  • SQL Server — encrypt, trustServerCertificate, trustStore.

The returned map is meant to be merged into the Properties passed to DriverManager.getConnection(String, java.util.Properties) — the driver reads its TLS settings from there, so no URL surgery is required. The method is pure (it only inspects the spec's path strings; it never opens the files), so it is fully unit-testable offline.

  • Method Details

    • forDriver

      public static Map<String,String> forDriver(String driverId, JdbcTlsSpec spec)
      Builds the TLS connection properties for driverId (the DriverInfo.id()). Returns an empty map when spec is empty or the driver needs no TLS (SQLite/H2) — or when the database is unknown.
